abrams-problem-statement: Introduction p.2: the paper defines its own problem (U, approximate eigenvector Va, true V and lambda_v).
abrams-locality-requirement: Sec. 3 p.5: the paper states the condition (sum of k-local terms, k independent of n) under which its method is meant to apply.
abrams-first-quantized-qubits: Sec. 3 p.6: the paper defines its own encoding (l qubits per particle, n*l qubits).
abrams-initial-state-from-classical-wave: Sec. 3 p.6: the paper states the input it requires (a classical wavefunction) and excludes density-functional methods.
abrams-open-problems-gates-errors: Conclusion p.8: the paper itself says gate counts and error analysis are left open.
aharonov-model-definition: Sec. 1 p.2 and Sec. 2.2 p.8: the paper defines the adiabatic model (Hinit, Hfinal, ground state of Hfinal as output, gap along the straight line).
aharonov-general-hfinal-scope: Sec. 1 p.2: the paper states that Hfinal is any local Hamiltonian (not only diagonal) and that this is what its results need.
aharonov-explicit-sparse-definition: Sec. 1.1 p.3: the paper defines explicit sparse Hamiltonians.
aharonov-six-state-open: Sec. 1.2 p.4: the paper states that six-state particles come from its construction and that improving this is open.
aharonov-noise-model-open: Sec. 1.2 p.4: the paper states that the right noise model and fault tolerance are not yet studied.
aharonov-five-body-interaction: Sec. 1.3 p.5 and Eq. (5) p.10: the paper's own Hamiltonian acts on three clock and two computation qubits.
aharonov-open-improve-parameters: Sec. 1.6 p.6: the paper states that better parameters (run time, particle dimension) are left open.
aharonov-open-one-dimensional: Sec. 1.6 p.6: the paper states that the one-dimensional case is left open.
aharonov-open-fault-tolerance: Sec. 1.6 p.6: the paper states that fault tolerance and physical usefulness are left open.
aharonov-open-adiabatic-optimization-pow: Sec. 1.6 p.6: the paper states that the power of adiabatic optimization is left open.
aharonov-spectral-gap-definition: Sec. 2.1 p.7: the paper defines the spectral gap, zero if the ground state is degenerate.
aharonov-k-local-restriction: Sec. 2.1 p.7: the paper states that it restricts itself to k-local Hamiltonians and tries to keep k small.
aharonov-definition-2-2-running-time: Definition 2.2, Sec. 2.2 p.8: the paper defines k-local adiabatic computation and its running time T*max||H(s)||.
aharonov-hamiltonian-construction-defini: Sec. 3.1.1 p.10: the paper defines Hinit, Hfinal and H(s) as sums of penalty terms.
aharonov-claim-3-2: Claim 3.2, Sec. 3.1.1 p.11: stated with its proof (Hinit|gamma0>=0 by direct check; sum of projectors is positive semidefinite).
aharonov-claim-3-3: Claim 3.3, Sec. 3.1.1 p.11: stated with its proof (Hfinal|eta>=0 by direct check, left to the reader as 'easy to verify'; each H_l is positive semidefinite).
aharonov-claim-3-7-monotone-ground-state: Claim 3.7, Sec. 3.1.2 p.13: stated with a proof (power-iteration limit, Perron's theorem which is textbook); preservation of monotonicity is stated as 'easy to check'.
aharonov-claim-3-8-conductance: Claim 3.8, Sec. 3.1.2 pp.13-14: stated with a case analysis proof using Claim 3.7; the conductance bound itself is applied after the claim.
aharonov-model-no-postprocessing: Sec. 3.1.3 p.14: the paper states that its model allows one adiabatic evolution and a measurement, with no classical postprocessing.
aharonov-lemma-3-10-identity-padding: Lemma 3.10, Sec. 3.1.3 p.15: stated with a proof (pad the circuit with identity gates, trace distance <= l2 distance, triangle inequality); the step 'easy to check' for the traced-out clock is short and elementary.
aharonov-three-local-penalty-j: Sec. 3.2.1 p.17: the paper sets the penalty J = epsilon^-2 L^6 and defines the 3-local Hamiltonians H'init, H'final.
aharonov-claim-3-16-restriction-equal: Claim 3.16, Sec. 3.2.2 p.18: stated with a direct proof (projection identity for each H_l).
aharonov-lemma-3-17-perturbation: Lemma 3.17, Sec. 3.2.2 pp.18-19: stated with its conditions (J>2K) and a full proof in the paper; the paper notes a similar lemma in [20] but proves this one.
aharonov-circuit-layout-assumption: Sec. 4.1 p.21: the paper states its circuit layout assumption (R rounds, L=2nR gates) and the padding it needs.
aharonov-six-state-particles-lattice: Sec. 4.2 p.21: the paper defines its 6-state particles, the four phases and the n x (R+1) lattice.

ajag-uc-random-instances: Sec. 4 p.20: randomly generated instances solved on D-Wave 2000Q and with Gurobi on the i7-6700.

ajag-hens-instance: Sec. 5 p.24: a random instance m=4, n=3, reformulated and solved on D-Wave and with Gurobi.
ajag-hens-discretization: Sec. 5.1 p.25: the paper states it discretized q_ij into N grid points chosen for least deviation.
ajag-hens-model-statistics: Table 5, Sec. 5.2 p.27: the paper's model statistics for m sources, n sinks and N grid points.

theory_low.abrams-fft-eigen-algorithm-claim: Abstract p.1 and Sec. 2 pp.3-5: an algorithm description and an authors' claim of polynomial time; no theorem and no proof of the complexity.
theory_low.abrams-running-time-overlap-condition: Introduction p.2: a claim of time proportional to 1/|<Va|V>|^2 and 1/epsilon, stated without proof. Footnote 2, p.5-6, says the total operation count scales as epsilon^-2, so the two statements do not agree.
theory_low.abrams-applies-to-any-poly-unitary: Sec. 2 p.3: an authors' claim that the algorithm applies to any polynomial-time U; no proof.
theory_low.abrams-controlled-power-loop: Sec. 2 p.4: a description of how U^j is built (a loop with a flag qubit) with 'implemented easily'; an algorithm sketch, no theorem or proof.
theory_low.abrams-fft-reveals-eigenphases: Sec. 2 p.4: 'self-evident' from Eq. (7); stated, not proved.
theory_low.abrams-fft-cost-and-accuracy: textbook, stated not proved (F129): Sec. 2 p.4 states the QFT cost poly(m) and accuracy linear in M with no derivation.
theory_low.abrams-measurement-probability: Sec. 2 p.4: a short argument with no theorem or proof statement; the poly-trials claim is stated, not proved.
theory_low.abrams-eigenvector-collapse: Sec. 2 p.4: stated as a consequence of measurement; no proof, no conditions.
theory_low.abrams-total-ops-scale-eps-minus-two: Footnote 2 pp.5-6: an informal argument that the cost scales as epsilon^-2; no proof, and it conflicts with the 1/epsilon in the Introduction.
theory_low.aharonov-abstract-equivalence: Abstract p.1: summary of Theorem 1.1, which is LOW (see that item).
theory_low.aharonov-theorem-1-1: Theorem 1.1, Sec. 1.1 p.3: one direction is cited to [13,9]; the other direction is Theorems 3.1/3.15, whose proofs use the cited Theorem 2.1 (adiabatic theorem), Sec. 2.2 p.8, is 'adapted from [29]' (Reichardt) and Lemma 3.14 (Kitaev's geometrical lemma, Lemma 14.4 in [22]), Sec. 3.1.4 p.16, is cited and not proved. Cited-step rule (a consequence of the rule, not a defect in the paper).
theory_low.aharonov-corollary-1-2: Corollary 1.2, Sec. 1.1 p.3: rests on Theorem 1.1 and on the result of [4] (cited, not proved here).
theory_low.aharonov-theorem-1-1-nonlocal-scope: Sec. 1.2 p.3: the first half (Theorem 1.1 uses 3-local terms between distant particles) is the paper's scope, but 'three-particle Hamiltonians are technologically very difficult to realize' is a field claim with no support. Weaker part wins.
theory_low.aharonov-theorem-1-3: Theorem 1.3, Sec. 1.2 p.4: proved as Theorem 4.1, which rests on the cited Theorem 2.1 (adiabatic theorem), Sec. 2.2 p.8, is 'adapted from [29]' (Reichardt) and on Lemma 3.12 (Lemma 3.14 (Kitaev's geometrical lemma, Lemma 14.4 in [22]), Sec. 3.1.4 p.16, is cited and not proved). Cited-step rule.
theory_low.aharonov-key-observation-nonnegligible-o: Sec. 1.3 p.4: an overview of the idea ('under some mild restrictions'); the formal statements are the later lemmas.
theory_low.aharonov-initial-hamiltonian-unique-grou: Sec. 1.3 p.5: an overview sentence; the formal statement is Theorem 3.1, which is LOW.
theory_low.aharonov-gap-via-markov-conductance: Sec. 1.3 p.5: an overview; the formal statement is Lemma 3.5, which is LOW.
theory_low.aharonov-output-extraction-clock-measure: Sec. 1.3 p.5 and footnote 4: an overview of output extraction; no proof here (see Lemma 3.10).
theory_low.aharonov-five-local-running-time-overvie: Sec. 1.3 p.5: 'roughly O(L^5)' is an overview figure; the exact bound is in Theorem 3.1, which is LOW.
theory_low.aharonov-three-local-running-time-overvi: Sec. 1.3 p.5: 'roughly O(L^14)' is an overview figure; the improvement to 3-locality is also credited to [20].
theory_low.aharonov-grid-snake-construction: Sec. 1.4 p.6: an overview of the Section 4 construction, not a proved statement.
theory_low.aharonov-invariant-subspace-stronger-bou: Sec. 2.2 p.9: a short informal justification ('follows from Schrodinger's equation'); not a numbered theorem.
theory_low.aharonov-general-models-also-hold: Sec. 2.2 p.9: 'Obviously' the main results hold for more general models; no proof.
theory_low.aharonov-fact-2-4-eigenvector-map: Fact 2.4, Sec. 2.3 p.9: 'easy to verify'; no proof in the paper.
theory_low.aharonov-theorem-3-1: Theorem 3.1, Sec. 3.1 p.10: proved through Claim 3.9, which uses the cited Theorem 2.1 (adiabatic theorem), Sec. 2.2 p.8, is 'adapted from [29]' (Reichardt). Cited-step rule. The text layer also garbles the middle of the statement.
theory_low.aharonov-claim-3-4-invariant-subspace: Claim 3.4, Sec. 3.1.2 p.11: 'easy to verify'; no proof in the paper.
theory_low.aharonov-lemma-3-5-gap-in-subspace: Lemma 3.5, Sec. 3.1.2 pp.11-14: the proof for s>=1/3 applies Theorem 2.5, the conductance bound of Sinclair-Jerrum [34], a specific cited theorem (Gerschgorin and Perron are textbook). Borderline: the conductance bound is also standard in Markov chain texts; the coordinator may upgrade.
theory_low.aharonov-claim-3-9-history-state: Claim 3.9, Sec. 3.1.3 p.14: the proof uses Lemma 3.5 (LOW) and the cited Theorem 2.1 (adiabatic theorem), Sec. 2.2 p.8, is 'adapted from [29]' (Reichardt). Cited-step rule.
theory_low.aharonov-history-state-measurement-proba: Sec. 3.1.3 p.14: an informal argument (probability 1/L, repeat O(L) times) that motivates Lemma 3.10; not a theorem.
theory_low.aharonov-lemma-3-11-full-space-gap: Lemma 3.11, Sec. 3.1.4 p.15: its proof uses Lemma 3.12, which uses the cited Lemma 3.14 (Kitaev's geometrical lemma, Lemma 14.4 in [22]), Sec. 3.1.4 p.16, is cited and not proved, and Lemma 3.5. Cited-step rule.
theory_low.aharonov-lemma-3-12-legal-clock-gap: Lemma 3.12, Sec. 3.1.4 pp.15-17: the proof uses Lemma 3.14 (Kitaev's geometrical lemma, Lemma 14.4 in [22]), Sec. 3.1.4 p.16, is cited and not proved, and Claim 3.13 ('easy to check').
theory_low.aharonov-claim-3-13-block-diagonal: Claim 3.13, Sec. 3.1.4 p.16: 'easy to check'; no proof in the paper.
theory_low.aharonov-theorem-3-15: Theorem 3.15, Sec. 3.2 p.17: the proof uses Lemmas 3.12, 3.18, 3.19 and the cited Theorem 2.1 (adiabatic theorem), Sec. 2.2 p.8, is 'adapted from [29]' (Reichardt). Cited-step rule.
theory_low.aharonov-three-local-history-not-exact-g: Sec. 3.2.1 p.18: the paper says the proof of Claim 3.3 does not apply and eta is no longer an exact ground state, without proof; the value's 'because the terms are no longer positive semidefinite' is not what the passage says.
theory_low.aharonov-lemma-3-18-three-local-gap: Lemma 3.18, Sec. 3.2.2 p.19: the proof applies Lemma 3.17 to the gap of Lemma 3.12, which rests on the cited Lemma 3.14 (Kitaev's geometrical lemma, Lemma 14.4 in [22]), Sec. 3.1.4 p.16, is cited and not proved.
theory_low.aharonov-lemma-3-19-final-ground-state-c: Lemma 3.19, Sec. 3.2.2 pp.19-20: the proof uses b-a=Omega(1/L^3) from Lemma 3.12, which rests on the cited Lemma 3.14 (Kitaev's geometrical lemma, Lemma 14.4 in [22]), Sec. 3.1.4 p.16, is cited and not proved.
theory_low.aharonov-three-local-running-time: Sec. 3.2.2 p.20: the bound follows from the cited Theorem 2.1 (adiabatic theorem), Sec. 2.2 p.8, is 'adapted from [29]' (Reichardt) and Lemmas 3.12, 3.19, 3.10; cited-step rule. The arithmetic is consistent.
theory_low.aharonov-theorem-4-1: Theorem 4.1, Sec. 4 p.20: the proof is 'essentially the same as' Sec. 3.2.2 and rests on the cited Theorem 2.1 (adiabatic theorem), Sec. 2.2 p.8, is 'adapted from [29]' (Reichardt) and on Lemma 3.12 (Lemma 3.14 (Kitaev's geometrical lemma, Lemma 14.4 in [22]), Sec. 3.1.4 p.16, is cited and not proved). Cited-step rule.
theory_low.aharonov-claim-4-2-legal-shapes: Claim 4.2, Sec. 4.4.1 p.24: the proof is an outline ending in 'easy to verify'; Table 1 is garbled in the text layer so its conditions cannot be checked.
theory_low.aharonov-two-site-propagation-property: Sec. 4.4.2 p.25: a design property of the construction, argued informally; not a numbered result.
theory_low.aharonov-lemma-4-6-grid-gap: Lemma 4.6, Sec. 4.5 p.27: the proof is one line reusing Lemma 3.12, which rests on the cited Lemma 3.14 (Kitaev's geometrical lemma, Lemma 14.4 in [22]), Sec. 3.1.4 p.16, is cited and not proved.
theory_low.aharonov-lemma-4-7-grid-full-gap: Lemma 4.7, Sec. 4.5 p.27: 'The proof is similar to' Lemmas 3.18 and 3.19; no proof given, and those are LOW.
theory_low.aharonov-grid-output-shape-measurement: Sec. 4.5 p.27: a sketch of a modification of Lemma 3.10 ('a minor modification still applies'); no proof.
theory_low.albash-theorem-1-jansen-ruskai-seiler: Theorem 1, Sec. II.B.1 p.7: stated and attributed to JRS (2007); the review says 'refer the reader to the original literature for their proofs'. Cited, not proved.
theory_low.albash-theorem-2-elgart-hagedorn: Theorem 2, Sec. II.B.2 p.8: stated and attributed to Elgart-Hagedorn (2012); proof not given. Cited, not proved.
theory_low.albash-theorem-3-ge-exponentially-small-: Theorem 3, Sec. II.B.3 p.8: stated and attributed to Ge et al. (2015); proof not given. Cited, not proved.
theory_low.albash-grover-linear-schedule-no-speedup: Sec. III.A.1 p.10: 'This suggests'; the conclusion comes from a sufficient condition (22), not a lower bound on the linear schedule.
theory_low.albash-grover-p2-sufficient-condition: Sec. III.A.2 p.11: the condition tf >> 2 pi sqrt(N)[1+log 2N] comes from the adiabatic condition (7)/(8)/(23), which is Theorem 1 of Jansen-Ruskai-Seiler (cited, proof not given), and from inequality (25), whose proof in Appendix A.2 drops an absolute value (see that item).
theory_low.albash-grover-local-schedule-quadratic: Sec. III.A.2 p.11: the integral (27)-(28) is calculus, but 'the expected quadratic speedup' needs a small adiabatic error; footnote 16 says it rests on a heuristic local condition and numerics.
theory_low.albash-grover-multi-marked-spectrum: Sec. III.A.3 p.12: the spectrum (33) is stated ('one finds') without derivation.
theory_low.albash-dj-unitary-interpolation-o1: Sec. III.B.1 pp.12-13: spectrum preservation is shown, but the O(1) run time rests on the adiabatic condition (7)/(8)/(23), which is Theorem 1 of Jansen-Ruskai-Seiler (cited, proof not given).
theory_low.albash-dj-linear-interpolation-o1: Sec. III.B.2 p.13: Lemma 1 is proved, but the O(1) run time follows from the adiabatic condition (8), i.e. the adiabatic condition (7)/(8)/(23), which is Theorem 1 of Jansen-Ruskai-Seiler (cited, proof not given).
theory_low.albash-bv-o1-runtime: Sec. III.C p.15: 'since only a single qubit is effectively evolving' is an informal argument; no gap or tf is computed (credited to Hen 2014b), and O(1) rests on an adiabatic condition. Argued informally.
theory_low.albash-glued-trees-almost-adiabatic: Sec. III.D p.15: the algorithm is Somma et al. (2012), cited; 'only example so far' is a survey claim. The 'almost' caveat is the review's own, but weaker parts win.
theory_low.albash-glued-trees-gap-structure: Sec. III.D pp.15-16: the c/n^3 bounds are Somma et al.'s and are not derived in the review (Fig. 2 is illustrative).
theory_low.albash-glued-trees-polynomial-time: Sec. III.D p.16: the schedule argument is a sketch ('we conclude'); the n^6 run time is not derived and rests on the cited Somma et al. gap bounds.
theory_low.albash-circuit-sim-product-2m-unitaries: Sec. IV.A p.19: the error bound is credited to van Dam et al. (2001) and the derivation is a sketch (Trotter-BCH, no full proof).
theory_low.albash-history-ground-states: Sec. IV.B p.20: the ground-state facts are proved in Appendix C.1-C.3, but 'the ground state is unique for s in [0,1]' in the whole space needs Appendix C.4, which uses the cited Geometrical Lemma (Kitaev et al.; Aharonov-Naveh).
theory_low.albash-history-gap-bounds: Sec. IV.B p.20: the bounds (79)-(80) rest on the conductance bound (Sinclair-Jerrum, cited) and, for the global gap, the cited Geometrical Lemma (Appendix C.4).
theory_low.albash-history-measurement-amplify: Sec. IV.B pp.20-21: the 1/(L+1) probability is stated; the amplification and the 'efficient implementation' claim rest on the gap bounds (79)-(80), which are LOW, and are not proved here.
theory_low.albash-mizel-gap-analysis-incomplete: Sec. IV.C p.21 and footnote 22: a statement about other papers' results (Mizel et al., Childs et al., Breuckmann-Terhal); a survey statement, not a result of this review.
theory_low.albash-lemma-2-nullspace-projection: Lemma 2, Sec. IV.C pp.21-22: stated and attributed to Childs et al. (2013); no proof given. Cited, not proved.
theory_low.albash-space-time-initial-ground-state: Sec. IV.D p.23: the ground state and eigenvalue 1 of H(0) are asserted without derivation, and Hinit in Eq. (88) is not a term of H(lambda) in Eq. (83).
theory_low.albash-space-time-four-body: Sec. IV.D p.23: the 4-body remark is the review's own, but the Lloyd-Terhal 2-local improvement is a cited result. Weaker part wins.
theory_low.albash-claim-1-ma-amplification: Claim 1, Sec. V.B p.27: attributed to others (Goldreich; Marriott-Watrous; Nagaj et al.); the Appendix D proof is incomplete (see appendix-d-amplification-proof).
theory_low.albash-no-theorem-rules-out-stoqaqc-spee: Sec. VI.B p.31: 'there does not exist a general theorem' is a claim about the whole literature, which the review cannot settle; the Monte Carlo remark is a field statement.
theory_low.albash-jordan-not-ground-state-universal: Sec. VI.C p.33: the caveat is the review's own, but the first half rests on the cited universality of H_ZZXX (Biamonte-Love; Sec. V.D). Weaker part wins.
theory_low.albash-hamming-overlap-exponentially-sma: Sec. VI.D.1 p.34, Eq. (112): the overlap bound is stated without derivation, and the 'we will show' part is covered by the next items.
theory_low.albash-hamming-exponential-time-conclusi: Sec. VI.D.1 p.35: the argument (credited to van Dam et al.) proves an exponentially small gap at sc; the review's own p.34 caveat says a small gap does not strictly imply exponential run time. The value overstates.
theory_low.albash-2sat-ring-minimum-gap: Sec. VI.D.2 pp.35-36, Eqs. (120)-(133): the gap formula is derived in the text, but 'which implies a polynomial run time' rests on adiabatic theorems (JRS, cited). Weaker part wins.
theory_low.albash-first-order-transition-not-always: Sec. VI.D.6 p.39: a field statement with citations (counterexamples known), not a result of this review.
theory_low.albash-stoqaqc-vs-sa-single-spin-only: Sec. VI.E p.40: the review's own caveat on single-spin SA is mixed with the cited claim that cluster-update SA can be significantly more efficient. Weaker part wins.
theory_low.albash-plain-hamming-weight-costs: Sec. VI.E.1 p.40: the O(sqrt n) quantum time and the O(n log n) SA bound are cited (Muthukrishnan et al., 2016); not derived here.
theory_low.albash-number-partitioning-encoding-prob: Sec. VI.F.1 p.41: a set of cited field statements (Hayes, Mertens, Garey-Johnson) with the authors' inference; not a result of this review.
theory_low.albash-exact-cover-speedup-open: Sec. VI.F.2 p.42: 'in all cases that have been studied to date' and 'no polynomial-time classical algorithm known' are survey claims about the field.
theory_low.albash-grover-tunneling-n-qubits: Sec. VI.G.1 pp.45-46: the potential (165) and Eq. (168) are shown, but 'tunneling of O(n) qubits' is an interpretation from the semiclassical picture and Fig. 8 numerics ('this potential suggests'). Argued informally.
theory_low.albash-structureless-final-hamiltonian-b: Sec. VII.A p.48, Eq. (183): 'one can show... [Theorem 2 of Farhi et al., 2008]'; stated and cited, no proof.
theory_low.albash-exponentially-small-gaps-not-rule: Sec. VII.G p.53: 'it is plausible' that the mechanism extends (citing Laumann et al.); a speculation with a cited basis.
theory_low.albash-dickson-perturbative-crossing-avo: Sec. VII.G p.54: 'it can be shown that higher order corrections do not depend on a' is not shown; the result is Dickson's (cited).
theory_low.albash-quantum-chemistry-aqc-unknown-gap: Sec. VIII pp.55-56: the mapping and the gadget reduction are cited claims, and the unknown gap scaling is a field statement.
theory_low.albash-appendix-a2-inequality-25: Appendix A.2 pp.56-57, Eqs. (A4)-(A5): the proof drops the absolute value on dDelta/dA between (A4b) and (A5a) (|d2A/ds2| has |dDelta/dA|), then uses that the integral of the derivative term vanishes from Delta(0)=Delta(1)=1. That holds only if Delta is monotone, and for Grover Delta dips to a minimum. Checked on the page image. Inequality (25) is not established as written.
theory_low.albash-appendix-b-grover-lower-bound: Appendix B p.57, Eqs. (B1)-(B10): the lower bound tf >= eps*(N-1)/(4 sqrt N) for a schedule independent of m is proved, but 'the locally optimised schedule is asymptotically optimal' needs the achievability of tf~sqrt(N), which footnote 16 (p.11) says is numerical (the rigorous bound has an extra log). Weaker part wins.
theory_low.albash-appendix-b-optimality-general: Appendix B footnote 40, p.57: the generalisation to arbitrary driving Hamiltonians is asserted without proof.
theory_low.albash-appendix-conductance-lower-bound: Appendix C.3.b p.60, Eqs. (C19)-(C24): the case analysis for F(B)/Pi(B) >= 1/(6L) is shown, but the gap bound applies the conductance bound of Sinclair-Jerrum (C13), a specific cited theorem. Borderline: also standard in Markov chain texts; the coordinator may upgrade.
theory_low.albash-appendix-global-gap-l-cubed: Appendix C.4 pp.60-61, Eq. (C29): the proof applies the Geometrical Lemma (Lemma 4; Aharonov-Naveh; Kitaev et al.), a cited lemma stated without proof.
theory_low.albash-appendix-d-amplification-proof: Appendix D pp.61-62: the first part (majority vote, multiplicative Chernoff, a textbook tool) is sound apart from a slip in the exponent of (D3) (a factor p). The second part (MA(c,c-1/|eta|^g)) defines no acceptance threshold (majority vote is wrong for c not 1/2) and omits completeness, so the proof is incomplete.
theory_low.albash-appendix-e1-perturbation-series-c: Appendix E.1 pp.62-63, Eqs. (E12)-(E17): the convergence bound is derived, but it builds on the expansion (E12)-(E13) of Bloch (1958), quoted ('it can be shown') and not derived.
theory_low.albash-appendix-e2-k-th-order-splitting: Appendix E.2 pp.64-65: shown explicitly only to second order; 'this argument extends to order k-1' is asserted, and it relies on the expansion of Bloch quoted in E.1.
theory_low.albash-appendix-e2-effective-hamiltonian: Appendix E.2 p.65, Eqs. (E29)-(E33): the leading-order coefficient is computed, but it relies on the Bloch expansion quoted in E.1 and the r-term case is 'the natural generalisation'.
theory_low.albash-appendix-e2-gadget-implementation: Appendix E.2 p.65: the strength mismatch is the review's own remark, but 'weaker gadgets exist' is a cited result (Cao and Nagaj, 2015). Weaker part wins.
